translations.kjv: And when they bring you unto the synagogues, and unto magistrates, and powers, take ye no thought how or what thing ye shall answer, or what ye shall say:
translations.ylt: `And when they bring you before the synagogues, and the rulers, and the authorities, be not anxious how or what ye may reply, or what ye may say,
translations.web: When they bring you before the synagogues, the rulers, and the authorities, don’t be anxious how or what you will answer or what you will say;

translations.kjv: For the Holy Ghost shall teach you in the same hour what ye ought to say.
translations.ylt: for the Holy Spirit shall teach you in that hour what it behoveth you to say.'
translations.web: for the Holy Spirit will teach you in that same hour what you must say.”

translations.kjv: And one of the company said unto him, Master, speak to my brother, that he divide the inheritance with me.
translations.ylt: And a certain one said to him, out of the multitude, `Teacher, say to my brother to divide with me the inheritance.'
translations.web: One of the multitude said to him, “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.”

translations.kjv: And he said unto him, Man, who made me a judge or a divider over you?
translations.ylt: And he said to him, `Man, who set me a judge or a divider over you?'
translations.web: But he said to him, “Man, who made me a judge or an arbitrator over you?”

translations.kjv: And he said unto them, Take heed, and beware of covetousness: for a man’s life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth.
translations.ylt: And he said unto them, `Observe, and beware of the covetousness, because not in the abundance of one's goods is his life.'
translations.web: He said to them, “Beware! Keep yourselves from covetousness, for a man’s life doesn’t consist of the abundance of the things which he possesses.”

translations.kjv: And he spake a parable unto them, saying, The ground of a certain rich man brought forth plentifully:
translations.ylt: And he spake a simile unto them, saying, `Of a certain rich man the field brought forth well;
translations.web: He spoke a parable to them, saying, “The ground of a certain rich man produced abundantly.

translations.kjv: And he thought within himself, saying, What shall I do, because I have no room where to bestow my fruits?
translations.ylt: and he was reasoning within himself, saying, What shall I do, because I have not where I shall gather together my fruits?
translations.web: He reasoned within himself, saying, ‘What will I do, because I don’t have room to store my crops?’

translations.kjv: And he said, This will I do: I will pull down my barns, and build greater; and there will I bestow all my fruits and my goods.
translations.ylt: and he said, This I will do, I will take down my storehouses, and greater ones I will build, and I will gather together there all my products and my good things,
translations.web: He said, ‘This is what I will do. I will pull down my barns, build bigger ones, and there I will store all my grain and my goods.

translations.kjv: And I will say to my soul, Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry.
translations.ylt: and I will say to my soul, Soul, thou hast many good things laid up for many years, be resting, eat, drink, be merry.
translations.web: I will tell my soul, “Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years. Take your ease, eat, drink, and be merry.”’

translations.kjv: But God said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?
translations.ylt: `And God said to him, Unthinking one! this night thy soul they shall require from thee, and what things thou didst prepare--to whom shall they be?
translations.web: “But God said to him, ‘You foolish one, tonight your soul is required of you. The things which you have prepared—whose will they be?’

translations.kjv: So is he that layeth up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.
translations.ylt: so is he who is treasuring up to himself, and is not rich toward God.'
translations.web: So is he who lays up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.”

translations.kjv: And he said unto his disciples, Therefore I say unto you, Take no thought for your life, what ye shall eat; neither for the body, what ye shall put on.
translations.ylt: And he said unto his disciples, `Because of this, to you I say, Be not anxious for your life, what ye may eat; nor for the body, what ye may put on;
translations.web: He said to his disciples, “Therefore I tell you, don’t be anxious for your life, what you will eat, nor yet for your body, what you will wear.

translations.kjv: The life is more than meat, and the body is more than raiment.
translations.ylt: the life is more than the nourishment, and the body than the clothing.
translations.web: Life is more than food, and the body is more than clothing.

translations.kjv: Consider the ravens: for they neither sow nor reap; which neither have storehouse nor barn; and God feedeth them: how much more are ye better than the fowls?
translations.ylt: `Consider the ravens, that they sow not, nor reap, to which there is no barn nor storehouse, and God doth nourish them; how much better are ye than the fowls?
translations.web: Consider the ravens: they don’t sow, they don’t reap, they have no warehouse or barn, and God feeds them. How much more valuable are you than birds!

translations.kjv: And which of you with taking thought can add to his stature one cubit?
translations.ylt: and who of you, being anxious, is able to add to his age one cubit?
translations.web: Which of you by being anxious can add a cubit to his height?

translations.kjv: If ye then be not able to do that thing which is least, why take ye thought for the rest?
translations.ylt: If, then, ye are not able for the least--why for the rest are ye anxious?
translations.web: If then you aren’t able to do even the least things, why are you anxious about the rest?

translations.kjv: Consider the lilies how they grow: they toil not, they spin not; and yet I say unto you, that Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.
translations.ylt: `Consider the lilies, how do they grow? they labour not, nor do they spin, and I say to you, not even Solomon in all his glory was arrayed as one of these;
translations.web: Consider the lilies, how they grow. They don’t toil, neither do they spin; yet I tell you, even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.

translations.kjv: If then God so clothe the grass, which is to day in the field, and to morrow is cast into the oven; how much more will he clothe you, O ye of little faith?
translations.ylt: and if the herbage in the field, that to-day is, and to-morrow into an oven is cast, God doth so clothe, how much more you--ye of little faith?
translations.web: But if this is how God clothes the grass in the field, which today exists and tomorrow is cast into the oven, how much more will he clothe you, O you of little faith?

translations.kjv: And seek not ye what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink, neither be ye of doubtful mind.
translations.ylt: `And ye--seek not what ye may eat, or what ye may drink, and be not in suspense,
translations.web: “Don’t seek what you will eat or what you will drink; neither be anxious.

translations.kjv: For all these things do the nations of the world seek after: and your Father knoweth that ye have need of these things.
translations.ylt: for all these things do the nations of the world seek after, and your Father hath known that ye have need of these things;
translations.web: For the nations of the world seek after all of these things, but your Father knows that you need these things.

translations.kjv: But rather seek ye the kingdom of God; and all these things shall be added unto you.
translations.ylt: but, seek ye the reign of God, and all these things shall be added to you.
translations.web: But seek God’s Kingdom, and all these things will be added to you.

translations.kjv: Fear not, little flock; for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the kingdom.
translations.ylt: `Fear not, little flock, because your Father did delight to give you the reign;
translations.web: “Don’t be afraid, little flock, for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the Kingdom.

translations.kjv: Sell that ye have, and give alms; provide yourselves bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that faileth not, where no thief approacheth, neither moth corrupteth.
translations.ylt: sell your goods, and give alms, make to yourselves bags that become not old, a treasure unfailing in the heavens, where thief doth not come near, nor moth destroy;
translations.web: Sell what you have and give gifts to the needy. Make for yourselves purses which don’t grow old, a treasure in the heavens that doesn’t fail, where no thief approaches and no moth destroys.

translations.kjv: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
translations.ylt: for where your treasure is, there also your heart will be.
translations.web: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.

translations.kjv: Let your loins be girded about, and your lights burning;
translations.ylt: `Let your loins be girded, and the lamps burning,
translations.web: “Let your waist be dressed and your lamps burning.

translations.kjv: And ye yourselves like unto men that wait for their lord, when he will return from the wedding; that when he cometh and knocketh, they may open unto him immediately.
translations.ylt: and ye like to men waiting for their lord, when he shall return out of the wedding feasts, that he having come and knocked, immediately they may open to him.
translations.web: Be like men watching for their lord when he returns from the wedding feast, that when he comes and knocks, they may immediately open to him.

translations.kjv: Blessed are those servants, whom the lord when he cometh shall find watching: verily I say unto you, that he shall gird himself, and make them to sit down to meat, and will come forth and serve them.
translations.ylt: `Happy those servants, whom the lord, having come, shall find watching; verily I say to you, that he will gird himself, and will cause them to recline (at meat), and having come near, will minister to them;
translations.web: Blessed are those servants whom the lord will find watching when he comes. Most certainly I tell you that he will dress himself, make them recline, and will come and serve them.

translations.kjv: And if he shall come in the second watch, or come in the third watch, and find them so, blessed are those servants.
translations.ylt: and if he may come in the second watch, and in the third watch he may come, and may find it so, happy are those servants.
translations.web: They will be blessed if he comes in the second or third watch and finds them so.

translations.kjv: And this know, that if the goodman of the house had known what hour the thief would come, he would have watched, and not have suffered his house to be broken through.
translations.ylt: `And this know, that if the master of the house had known what hour the thief doth come, he would have watched, and would not have suffered his house to be broken through;
translations.web: But know this, that if the master of the house had known in what hour the thief was coming, he would have watched and not allowed his house to be broken into.

translations.kjv: Be ye therefore ready also: for the Son of man cometh at an hour when ye think not.
translations.ylt: and ye, then, become ye ready, because at the hour ye think not, the Son of Man doth come.'
translations.web: Therefore be ready also, for the Son of Man is coming in an hour that you don’t expect him.”

translations.kjv: Then Peter said unto him, Lord, speakest thou this parable unto us, or even to all?
translations.ylt: And Peter said to him, `Sir, unto us this simile dost thou speak, or also unto all?'
translations.web: Peter said to him, “Lord, are you telling this parable to us, or to everybody?”

translations.kjv: And the Lord said, Who then is that faithful and wise steward, whom his lord shall make ruler over his household, to give them their portion of meat in due season?
translations.ylt: And the Lord said, `Who, then, is the faithful and prudent steward whom the lord shall set over his household, to give in season the wheat measure?
translations.web: The Lord said, “Who then is the faithful and wise steward, whom his lord will set over his household, to give them their portion of food at the right times?

translations.kjv: Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he cometh shall find so doing.
translations.ylt: Happy that servant, whom his lord, having come, shall find doing so;
translations.web: Blessed is that servant whom his lord will find doing so when he comes.

translations.kjv: Of a truth I say unto you, that he will make him ruler over all that he hath.
translations.ylt: truly I say to you, that over all his goods he will set him.
translations.web: Truly I tell you that he will set him over all that he has.

translations.kjv: But and if that servant say in his heart, My lord delayeth his coming; and shall begin to beat the menservants and maidens, and to eat and drink, and to be drunken;
translations.ylt: `And if that servant may say in his heart, My lord doth delay to come, and may begin to beat the men-servants and the maid-servants, to eat also, and to drink, and to be drunken;
translations.web: But if that servant says in his heart, ‘My lord delays his coming,’ and begins to beat the menservants and the maidservants, and to eat and drink and to be drunken,

translations.kjv: The lord of that servant will come in a day when he looketh not for him, and at an hour when he is not aware, and will cut him in sunder, and will appoint him his portion with the unbelievers.
translations.ylt: the lord of that servant will come in a day in which he doth not look for him, and in an hour that he doth not know, and will cut him off, and his portion with the unfaithful he will appoint.
translations.web: then the lord of that servant will come in a day when he isn’t expecting him and in an hour that he doesn’t know, and will cut him in two, and place his portion with the unfaithful.

translations.kjv: And that servant, which knew his lord’s will, and prepared not himself, neither did according to his will, shall be beaten with many stripes.
translations.ylt: `And that servant, who having known his lord's will, and not having prepared, nor having gone according to his will, shall be beaten with many stripes,
translations.web: That servant who knew his lord’s will, and didn’t prepare nor do what he wanted, will be beaten with many stripes,

translations.kjv: But he that knew not, and did commit things worthy of stripes, shall be beaten with few stripes. For unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required: and to whom men have committed much, of him they will ask the more.
translations.ylt: and he who, not having known, and having done things worthy of stripes, shall be beaten with few; and to every one to whom much was given, much shall be required from him; and to whom they did commit much, more abundantly they will ask of him.
translations.web: but he who didn’t know, and did things worthy of stripes, will be beaten with few stripes. To whomever much is given, of him will much be required; and to whom much was entrusted, of him more will be asked.

translations.kjv: I am come to send fire on the earth; and what will I, if it be already kindled?
translations.ylt: `Fire I came to cast to the earth, and what will I if already it was kindled?
translations.web: “I came to throw fire on the earth. I wish it were already kindled.

translations.kjv: But I have a baptism to be baptized with; and how am I straitened till it be accomplished!
translations.ylt: but I have a baptism to be baptized with, and how am I pressed till it may be completed!
translations.web: But I have a baptism to be baptized with, and how distressed I am until it is accomplished!

translations.kjv: Suppose ye that I am come to give peace on earth? I tell you, Nay; but rather division:
translations.ylt: `Think ye that peace I came to give in the earth? no, I say to you, but rather division;
translations.web: Do you think that I have come to give peace on the earth? I tell you, no, but rather division.

translations.kjv: For from henceforth there shall be five in one house divided, three against two, and two against three.
translations.ylt: for there shall be henceforth five in one house divided--three against two, and two against three;
translations.web: For from now on, there will be five in one house divided, three against two, and two against three.

translations.kjv: The father shall be divided against the son, and the son against the father; the mother against the daughter, and the daughter against the mother; the mother in law against her daughter in law, and the daughter in law against her mother in law.
translations.ylt: a father shall be divided against a son, and a son against a father, a mother against a daughter, and a daughter against a mother, a mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.'
translations.web: They will be divided, father against son, and son against father; mother against daughter, and daughter against her mother; mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law, and daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.”

translations.kjv: And he said also to the people, When ye see a cloud rise out of the west, straightway ye say, There cometh a shower; and so it is.
translations.ylt: And he said also to the multitudes, `When ye may see the cloud rising from the west, immediately ye say, A shower doth come, and it is so;
translations.web: He said to the multitudes also, “When you see a cloud rising from the west, immediately you say, ‘A shower is coming,’ and so it happens.

translations.kjv: And when ye see the south wind blow, ye say, There will be heat; and it cometh to pass.
translations.ylt: and when--a south wind blowing, ye say, that there will be heat, and it is;
translations.web: When a south wind blows, you say, ‘There will be a scorching heat,’ and it happens.

translations.kjv: Ye hypocrites, ye can discern the face of the sky and of the earth; but how is it that ye do not discern this time?
translations.ylt: hypocrites! the face of the earth and of the heaven ye have known to make proof of, but this time--how do ye not make proof of it?
translations.web: You hypocrites! You know how to interpret the appearance of the earth and the sky, but how is it that you don’t interpret this time?

translations.kjv: Yea, and why even of yourselves judge ye not what is right?
translations.ylt: `And why, also, of yourselves, judge ye not what is righteous?
translations.web: “Why don’t you judge for yourselves what is right?

translations.kjv: When thou goest with thine adversary to the magistrate, as thou art in the way, give diligence that thou mayest be delivered from him; lest he hale thee to the judge, and the judge deliver thee to the officer, and the officer cast thee into prison.
translations.ylt: for, as thou art going away with thy opponent to the ruler, in the way give diligence to be released from him, lest he may drag thee unto the judge, and the judge may deliver thee to the officer, and the officer may cast thee into prison;
translations.web: For when you are going with your adversary before the magistrate, try diligently on the way to be released from him, lest perhaps he drag you to the judge, and the judge deliver you to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.

translations.kjv: I tell thee, thou shalt not depart thence, till thou hast paid the very last mite.
translations.ylt: I say to thee, thou mayest not come forth thence till even the last mite thou mayest give back.'
translations.web: I tell you, you will by no means get out of there until you have paid the very last penny.”

translations.kjv: There were present at that season some that told him of the Galileans, whose blood Pilate had mingled with their sacrifices.
translations.ylt: And there were present certain at that time, telling him about the Galileans, whose blood Pilate did mingle with their sacrifices;
translations.web: Now there were some present at the same time who told him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.

translations.kjv: And Jesus answering said unto them, Suppose ye that these Galileans were sinners above all the Galileans, because they suffered such things?
translations.ylt: and Jesus answering said to them, `Think ye that these Galileans became sinners beyond all the Galileans, because they have suffered such things?
translations.web: Jesus answered them, “Do you think that these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans, because they suffered such things?

translations.kjv: I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.
translations.ylt: No--I say to you, but, if ye may not reform, all ye even so shall perish.
translations.web: I tell you, no, but unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.

translations.kjv: Or those eighteen, upon whom the tower in Siloam fell, and slew them, think ye that they were sinners above all men that dwelt in Jerusalem?
translations.ylt: `Or those eighteen, on whom the tower in Siloam fell, and killed them; think ye that these became debtors beyond all men who are dwelling in Jerusalem?
translations.web: Or those eighteen on whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them—do you think that they were worse offenders than all the men who dwell in Jerusalem?

translations.kjv: I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.
translations.ylt: No--I say to you, but, if ye may not reform, all ye in like manner shall perish.'
translations.web: I tell you, no, but, unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.”

translations.kjv: He spake also this parable; A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard; and he came and sought fruit thereon, and found none.
translations.ylt: And he spake this simile: `A certain one had a fig-tree planted in his vineyard, and he came seeking fruit in it, and he did not find;
translations.web: He spoke this parable. “A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came seeking fruit on it and found none.

translations.kjv: Then said he unto the dresser of his vineyard, Behold, these three years I come seeking fruit on this fig tree, and find none: cut it down; why cumbereth it the ground?
translations.ylt: and he said unto the vine-dresser, Lo, three years I come seeking fruit in this fig-tree, and do not find, cut it off, why also the ground doth it render useless?
translations.web: He said to the vine dresser, ‘Behold, these three years I have come looking for fruit on this fig tree, and found none. Cut it down! Why does it waste the soil?’

translations.kjv: And he answering said unto him, Lord, let it alone this year also, till I shall dig about it, and dung it:
translations.ylt: `And he answering saith to him, Sir, suffer it also this year, till that I may dig about it, and cast in dung;
translations.web: He answered, ‘Lord, leave it alone this year also, until I dig around it and fertilize it.

translations.kjv: And if it bear fruit, well: and if not, then after that thou shalt cut it down.
translations.ylt: and if indeed it may bear fruit--;and if not so, thereafter thou shalt cut it off.'
translations.web: If it bears fruit, fine; but if not, after that, you can cut it down.’”

translations.kjv: And he was teaching in one of the synagogues on the sabbath.
translations.ylt: And he was teaching in one of the synagogues on the sabbath,
translations.web: He was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath day.

translations.kjv: And, behold, there was a woman which had a spirit of infirmity eighteen years, and was bowed together, and could in no wise lift up herself.
translations.ylt: and lo, there was a woman having a spirit of infirmity eighteen years, and she was bowed together, and not able to bend back at all,
translations.web: Behold, there was a woman who had a spirit of infirmity eighteen years. She was bent over and could in no way straighten herself up.

translations.kjv: And when Jesus saw her, he called her to him, and said unto her, Woman, thou art loosed from thine infirmity.
translations.ylt: and Jesus having seen her, did call her near, and said to her, `Woman, thou hast been loosed from thy infirmity;'
translations.web: When Jesus saw her, he called her and said to her, “Woman, you are freed from your infirmity.”

translations.kjv: And he laid his hands on her: and immediately she was made straight, and glorified God.
translations.ylt: and he laid on her his hands, and presently she was set upright, and was glorifying God.
translations.web: He laid his hands on her, and immediately she stood up straight and glorified God.

translations.kjv: And the ruler of the synagogue answered with indignation, because that Jesus had healed on the sabbath day, and said unto the people, There are six days in which men ought to work: in them therefore come and be healed, and not on the sabbath day.
translations.ylt: And the chief of the synagogue answering--much displeased that on the sabbath Jesus healed--said to the multitude, `Six days there are in which it behoveth us to be working; in these, then, coming, be healed, and not on the sabbath-day.'
translations.web: The ruler of the synagogue, being indignant because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, said to the multitude, “There are six days in which men ought to work. Therefore come on those days and be healed, and not on the Sabbath day!”

translations.kjv: The Lord then answered him, and said, Thou hypocrite, doth not each one of you on the sabbath loose his ox or his ass from the stall, and lead him away to watering?
translations.ylt: Then the Lord answered him and said, `Hypocrite, doth not each of you on the sabbath loose his ox or ass from the stall, and having led away, doth water it?
translations.web: Therefore the Lord answered him, “You hypocrites! Doesn’t each one of you free his ox or his donkey from the stall on the Sabbath and lead him away to water?

translations.kjv: And ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan hath bound, lo, these eighteen years, be loosed from this bond on the sabbath day?
translations.ylt: and this one, being a daughter of Abraham, whom the Adversary bound, lo, eighteen years, did it not behove to be loosed from this bond on the sabbath-day?'
translations.web: Ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham whom Satan had bound eighteen long years, be freed from this bondage on the Sabbath day?”

translations.kjv: And when he had said these things, all his adversaries were ashamed: and all the people rejoiced for all the glorious things that were done by him.
translations.ylt: And he saying these things, all who were opposed to him were being ashamed, and all the multitude were rejoicing over all the glorious things that are being done by him.
translations.web: As he said these things, all his adversaries were disappointed; and all the multitude rejoiced for all the glorious things that were done by him.

translations.kjv: Then said he, Unto what is the kingdom of God like? and whereunto shall I resemble it?
translations.ylt: And he said, `To what is the reign of God like? and to what shall I liken it?
translations.web: He said, “What is God’s Kingdom like? To what shall I compare it?

translations.kjv: It is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and cast into his garden; and it grew, and waxed a great tree; and the fowls of the air lodged in the branches of it.
translations.ylt: It is like to a grain of mustard, which a man having taken, did cast into his garden, and it increased, and came to a great tree, and the fowls of the heavens did rest in its branches.'
translations.web: It is like a grain of mustard seed which a man took and put in his own garden. It grew and became a large tree, and the birds of the sky live in its branches.”

translations.kjv: And again he said, Whereunto shall I liken the kingdom of God?
translations.ylt: And again he said, `To what shall I liken the reign of God?
translations.web: Again he said, “To what shall I compare God’s Kingdom?

translations.kjv: It is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened.
translations.ylt: It is like leaven, which a woman, having taken, did hide in three measures of meal, till that all was leavened.'
translations.web: It is like yeast, which a woman took and hid in three measures of flour, until it was all leavened.”

translations.kjv: And he went through the cities and villages, teaching, and journeying toward Jerusalem.
translations.ylt: And he was going through cities and villages, teaching, and making progress toward Jerusalem;
translations.web: He went on his way through cities and villages, teaching, and traveling on to Jerusalem.

translations.kjv: Then said one unto him, Lord, are there few that be saved? And he said unto them,
translations.ylt: and a certain one said to him, `Sir, are those saved few?' and he said unto them,
translations.web: One said to him, “Lord, are they few who are saved?” He said to them,

translations.kjv: Strive to enter in at the strait gate: for many, I say unto you, will seek to enter in, and shall not be able.
translations.ylt: `Be striving to go in through the straight gate, because many, I say to you, will seek to go in, and shall not be able;
translations.web: “Strive to enter in by the narrow door, for many, I tell you, will seek to enter in and will not be able.

translations.kjv: When once the master of the house is risen up, and hath shut to the door, and ye begin to stand without, and to knock at the door, saying, Lord, Lord, open unto us; and he shall answer and say unto you, I know you not whence ye are:
translations.ylt: from the time the master of the house may have risen up, and may have shut the door, and ye may begin without to stand, and to knock at the door, saying, Lord, lord, open to us, and he answering shall say to you, I have not known you whence ye are,
translations.web: When once the master of the house has risen up and has shut the door, and you begin to stand outside and to knock at the door, saying, ‘Lord, Lord, open to us!’ then he will answer and tell you, ‘I don’t know you or where you come from.’

translations.kjv: Then shall ye begin to say, We have eaten and drunk in thy presence, and thou hast taught in our streets.
translations.ylt: then ye may begin to say, We did eat before thee, and did drink, and in our broad places thou didst teach;
translations.web: Then you will begin to say, ‘We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught in our streets.’

translations.kjv: But he shall say, I tell you, I know you not whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity.
translations.ylt: and he shall say, I say to you, I have not known you whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of the unrighteousness.
translations.web: He will say, ‘I tell you, I don’t know where you come from. Depart from me, all you workers of iniquity.’

translations.kjv: There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when ye shall see Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, in the kingdom of God, and you yourselves thrust out.
translations.ylt: `There shall be there the weeping and the gnashing of the teeth, when ye may see Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, in the reign of God, and yourselves being cast out without;
translations.web: There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in God’s Kingdom, and yourselves being thrown outside.

translations.kjv: And they shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and shall sit down in the kingdom of God.
translations.ylt: and they shall come from east and west, and from north and south, and shall recline in the reign of God,
translations.web: They will come from the east, west, north, and south, and will sit down in God’s Kingdom.

translations.kjv: And, behold, there are last which shall be first, and there are first which shall be last.
translations.ylt: and lo, there are last who shall be first, and there are first who shall be last.'
translations.web: Behold, there are some who are last who will be first, and there are some who are first who will be last.”

translations.kjv: The same day there came certain of the Pharisees, saying unto him, Get thee out, and depart hence: for Herod will kill thee.
translations.ylt: On that day there came near certain Pharisees, saying to him, `Go forth, and be going on hence, for Herod doth wish to kill thee;'
translations.web: On that same day, some Pharisees came, saying to him, “Get out of here and go away, for Herod wants to kill you.”

translations.kjv: And he said unto them, Go ye, and tell that fox, Behold, I cast out devils, and I do cures to day and to morrow, and the third day I shall be perfected.
translations.ylt: and he said to them, `Having gone, say to this fox, Lo, I cast forth demons, and perfect cures to-day and to-morrow, and the third day I am being perfected;
translations.web: He said to them, “Go and tell that fox, ‘Behold, I cast out demons and perform cures today and tomorrow, and the third day I complete my mission.

translations.kjv: Nevertheless I must walk to day, and to morrow, and the day following: for it cannot be that a prophet perish out of Jerusalem.
translations.ylt: but it behoveth me to-day, and to-morrow, and the day following, to go on, because it is not possible for a prophet to perish out of Jerusalem.
translations.web: Nevertheless I must go on my way today and tomorrow and the next day, for it can’t be that a prophet would perish outside of Jerusalem.’

translations.kjv: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, which killest the prophets, and stonest them that are sent unto thee; how often would I have gathered thy children together, as a hen doth gather her brood under her wings, and ye would not!
translations.ylt: `Jerusalem, Jerusalem, that is killing the prophets, and stoning those sent unto her, how often did I will to gather together thy children, as a hen her brood under the wings, and ye did not will.
translations.web: “Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to her! How often I wanted to gather your children together, like a hen gathers her own brood under her wings, and you refused!

translations.kjv: Behold, your house is left unto you desolate: and verily I say unto you, Ye shall not see me, until the time come when ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.
translations.ylt: `Lo, your house is being left to you desolate, and verily I say to you--ye may not see me, till it may come, when ye may say, Blessed is he who is coming in the name of the Lord.'
translations.web: Behold, your house is left to you desolate. I tell you, you will not see me until you say, ‘Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!’”

translations.kjv: And it came to pass, as he went into the house of one of the chief Pharisees to eat bread on the sabbath day, that they watched him.
translations.ylt: And it came to pass, on his going into the house of a certain one of the chiefs of the Pharisees, on a sabbath, to eat bread, that they were watching him,
translations.web: When he went into the house of one of the rulers of the Pharisees on a Sabbath to eat bread, they were watching him.

translations.kjv: And, behold, there was a certain man before him which had the dropsy.
translations.ylt: and lo, there was a certain dropsical man before him;
translations.web: Behold, a certain man who had dropsy was in front of him.

translations.kjv: And Jesus answering spake unto the lawyers and Pharisees, saying, Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath day?
translations.ylt: and Jesus answering spake to the lawyers and Pharisees, saying, `Is it lawful on the sabbath-day to heal?'
translations.web: Jesus, answering, spoke to the lawyers and Pharisees, saying, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?”

translations.kjv: And they held their peace. And he took him, and healed him, and let him go;
translations.ylt: and they were silent, and having taken hold of him, he healed him, and let him go;
translations.web: But they were silent. He took him, and healed him, and let him go.

translations.kjv: And answered them, saying, Which of you shall have an ass or an ox fallen into a pit, and will not straightway pull him out on the sabbath day?
translations.ylt: and answering them he said, `Of which of you shall an ass or ox fall into a pit, and he will not immediately draw it up on the sabbath-day?'
translations.web: He answered them, “Which of you, if your son or an ox fell into a well, wouldn’t immediately pull him out on a Sabbath day?”

translations.kjv: And they could not answer him again to these things.
translations.ylt: and they were not able to answer him again unto these things.
translations.web: They couldn’t answer him regarding these things.

translations.kjv: And he put forth a parable to those which were bidden, when he marked how they chose out the chief rooms; saying unto them,
translations.ylt: And he spake a simile unto those called, marking how they were choosing out the first couches, saying unto them,
translations.web: He spoke a parable to those who were invited, when he noticed how they chose the best seats, and said to them,

translations.kjv: When thou art bidden of any man to a wedding, sit not down in the highest room; lest a more honourable man than thou be bidden of him;
translations.ylt: `When thou mayest be called by any one to marriage-feasts, thou mayest not recline on the first couch, lest a more honourable than thou may have been called by him,
translations.web: “When you are invited by anyone to a wedding feast, don’t sit in the best seat, since perhaps someone more honorable than you might be invited by him,

translations.kjv: And he that bade thee and him come and say to thee, Give this man place; and thou begin with shame to take the lowest room.
translations.ylt: and he who did call thee and him having come shall say to thee, Give to this one place, and then thou mayest begin with shame to occupy the last place.
translations.web: and he who invited both of you would come and tell you, ‘Make room for this person.’ Then you would begin, with shame, to take the lowest place.

translations.kjv: But when thou art bidden, go and sit down in the lowest room; that when he that bade thee cometh, he may say unto thee, Friend, go up higher: then shalt thou have worship in the presence of them that sit at meat with thee.
translations.ylt: `But, when thou mayest be called, having gone on, recline in the last place, that when he who called thee may come, he may say to thee, Friend, come up higher; then thou shalt have glory before those reclining with thee;
translations.web: But when you are invited, go and sit in the lowest place, so that when he who invited you comes, he may tell you, ‘Friend, move up higher.’ Then you will be honored in the presence of all who sit at the table with you.

translations.kjv: For whosoever exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.
translations.ylt: because every one who is exalting himself shall be humbled, and he who is humbling himself shall be exalted.'
translations.web: For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.”

translations.kjv: Then said he also to him that bade him, When thou makest a dinner or a supper, call not thy friends, nor thy brethren, neither thy kinsmen, nor thy rich neighbours; lest they also bid thee again, and a recompence be made thee.
translations.ylt: And he said also to him who did call him, `When thou mayest make a dinner or a supper, be not calling thy friends, nor thy brethren, nor thy kindred, nor rich neighbours, lest they may also call thee again, and a recompense may come to thee;
translations.web: He also said to the one who had invited him, “When you make a dinner or a supper, don’t call your friends, nor your brothers, nor your kinsmen, nor rich neighbors, or perhaps they might also return the favor, and pay you back.

translations.kjv: But when thou makest a feast, call the poor, the maimed, the lame, the blind:
translations.ylt: but when thou mayest make a feast, be calling poor, maimed, lame, blind,
translations.web: But when you make a feast, ask the poor, the maimed, the lame, or the blind;

translations.kjv: And thou shalt be blessed; for they cannot recompense thee: for thou shalt be recompensed at the resurrection of the just.
translations.ylt: and happy thou shalt be, because they have not to recompense thee, for it shall be recompensed to thee in the rising again of the righteous.'
translations.web: and you will be blessed, because they don’t have the resources to repay you. For you will be repaid in the resurrection of the righteous.”

translations.kjv: And when one of them that sat at meat with him heard these things, he said unto him, Blessed is he that shall eat bread in the kingdom of God.
translations.ylt: And one of those reclining with him, having heard these things, said to him, `Happy is he who shall eat bread in the reign of God;'
translations.web: When one of those who sat at the table with him heard these things, he said to him, “Blessed is he who will feast in God’s Kingdom!”

translations.kjv: Then said he unto him, A certain man made a great supper, and bade many:
translations.ylt: and he said to him, `A certain man made a great supper, and called many,
translations.web: But he said to him, “A certain man made a great supper, and he invited many people.

translations.kjv: And sent his servant at supper time to say to them that were bidden, Come; for all things are now ready.
translations.ylt: and he sent his servant at the hour of the supper to say to those having been called, Be coming, because now are all things ready.
translations.web: He sent out his servant at supper time to tell those who were invited, ‘Come, for everything is ready now.’

translations.kjv: And they all with one consent began to make excuse. The first said unto him, I have bought a piece of ground, and I must needs go and see it: I pray thee have me excused.
translations.ylt: `And they began with one consent all to excuse themselves: The first said to him, A field I bought, and I have need to go forth and see it; I beg of thee, have me excused.
translations.web: They all as one began to make excuses. “The first said to him, ‘I have bought a field, and I must go and see it. Please have me excused.’

translations.kjv: And another said, I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I go to prove them: I pray thee have me excused.
translations.ylt: `And another said, Five yoke of oxen I bought, and I go on to prove them; I beg of thee, have me excused:
translations.web: “Another said, ‘I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I must go try them out. Please have me excused.’

translations.kjv: And another said, I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come.
translations.ylt: and another said, A wife I married, and because of this I am not able to come.
translations.web: “Another said, ‘I have married a wife, and therefore I can’t come.’

translations.kjv: So that servant came, and shewed his lord these things. Then the master of the house being angry said to his servant, Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in hither the poor, and the maimed, and the halt, and the blind.
translations.ylt: `And that servant having come, told to his lord these things, then the master of the house, having been angry, said to his servant, Go forth quickly to the broad places and lanes of the city, and the poor, and maimed, and lame, and blind, bring in hither.
translations.web: “That servant came, and told his lord these things. Then the master of the house, being angry, said to his servant, ‘Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in the poor, maimed, blind, and lame.’

translations.kjv: And the servant said, Lord, it is done as thou hast commanded, and yet there is room.
translations.ylt: `And the servant said, Sir, it hath been done as thou didst command, and still there is room.
translations.web: “The servant said, ‘Lord, it is done as you commanded, and there is still room.’

translations.kjv: And the lord said unto the servant, Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.
translations.ylt: `And the lord said unto the servant, Go forth to the ways and hedges, and constrain to come in, that my house may be filled;
translations.web: “The lord said to the servant, ‘Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.

translations.kjv: For I say unto you, That none of those men which were bidden shall taste of my supper.
translations.ylt: for I say to you, that none of those men who have been called shall taste of my supper.'
translations.web: For I tell you that none of those men who were invited will taste of my supper. For many are called, but few are chosen.’”

translations.kjv: And there went great multitudes with him: and he turned, and said unto them,
translations.ylt: And there were going on with him great multitudes, and having turned, he said unto them,
translations.web: Now great multitudes were going with him. He turned and said to them,

translations.kjv: If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple.
translations.ylt: `If any one doth come unto me, and doth not hate his own father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brothers, and sisters, and yet even his own life, he is not able to be my disciple;
translations.web: “If anyone comes to me, and doesn’t disregard his own father, mother, wife, children, brothers, and sisters, yes, and his own life also, he can’t be my disciple.

translations.kjv: And whosoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple.
translations.ylt: and whoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, is not able to be my disciple.
translations.web: Whoever doesn’t bear his own cross and come after me, can’t be my disciple.

translations.kjv: For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it?
translations.ylt: `For who of you, willing to build a tower, doth not first, having sat down, count the expence, whether he have the things for completing?
translations.web: For which of you, desiring to build a tower, doesn’t first sit down and count the cost, to see if he has enough to complete it?

translations.kjv: Lest haply, after he hath laid the foundation, and is not able to finish it, all that behold it begin to mock him,
translations.ylt: lest that he having laid a foundation, and not being able to finish, all who are beholding may begin to mock him,
translations.web: Or perhaps, when he has laid a foundation and isn’t able to finish, everyone who sees begins to mock him,

translations.kjv: Saying, This man began to build, and was not able to finish.
translations.ylt: saying--This man began to build, and was not able to finish.
translations.web: saying, ‘This man began to build and wasn’t able to finish.’

translations.kjv: Or what king, going to make war against another king, sitteth not down first, and consulteth whether he be able with ten thousand to meet him that cometh against him with twenty thousand?
translations.ylt: `Or what king going on to engage with another king in war, doth not, having sat down, first consult if he be able with ten thousand to meet him who with twenty thousand is coming against him?
translations.web: Or what king, as he goes to encounter another king in war, will not sit down first and consider whether he is able with ten thousand to meet him who comes against him with twenty thousand?

translations.kjv: Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sendeth an ambassage, and desireth conditions of peace.
translations.ylt: and if not so--he being yet a long way off--having sent an embassy, he doth ask the things for peace.
translations.web: Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sends an envoy and asks for conditions of peace.

translations.kjv: So likewise, whosoever he be of you that forsaketh not all that he hath, he cannot be my disciple.
translations.ylt: `So, then, every one of you who doth not take leave of all that he himself hath, is not able to be my disciple.
translations.web: So therefore, whoever of you who doesn’t renounce all that he has, he can’t be my disciple.

translations.kjv: Salt is good: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be seasoned?
translations.ylt: `The salt is good, but if the salt doth become tasteless, with what shall it be seasoned?
translations.web: “Salt is good, but if the salt becomes flat and tasteless, with what do you season it?

translations.kjv: It is neither fit for the land, nor yet for the dunghill; but men cast it out. He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.
translations.ylt: neither for land nor for manure is it fit--they cast it without. He who is having ears to hear--let him hear.'
translations.web: It is fit neither for the soil nor for the manure pile. It is thrown out. He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”

translations.kjv: Then drew near unto him all the publicans and sinners for to hear him.
translations.ylt: And all the tax-gatherers and the sinners were coming nigh to him, to hear him,
translations.web: Now all the tax collectors and sinners were coming close to him to hear him.

translations.kjv: And the Pharisees and scribes murmured, saying, This man receiveth sinners, and eateth with them.
translations.ylt: and the Pharisees and the scribes were murmuring, saying--This one doth receive sinners, and doth eat with them.'
translations.web: The Pharisees and the scribes murmured, saying, “This man welcomes sinners, and eats with them.”

translations.kjv: And he spake this parable unto them, saying,
translations.ylt: And he spake unto them this simile, saying,
translations.web: He told them this parable:

translations.kjv: What man of you, having an hundred sheep, if he lose one of them, doth not leave the ninety and nine in the wilderness, and go after that which is lost, until he find it?
translations.ylt: `What man of you having a hundred sheep, and having lost one out of them, doth not leave behind the ninety-nine in the wilderness, and go on after the lost one, till he may find it?
translations.web: “Which of you men, if you had one hundred sheep and lost one of them, wouldn’t leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the one that was lost, until he found it?

translations.kjv: And when he hath found it, he layeth it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
translations.ylt: and having found, he doth lay it on his shoulders rejoicing,
translations.web: When he has found it, he carries it on his shoulders, rejoicing.

translations.kjv: And when he cometh home, he calleth together his friends and neighbours, saying unto them, Rejoice with me; for I have found my sheep which was lost.
translations.ylt: and having come to the house, he doth call together the friends and the neighbours, saying to them, Rejoice with me, because I found my sheep--the lost one.
translations.web: When he comes home, he calls together his friends and his neighbors, saying to them, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep which was lost!’

translations.kjv: I say unto you, that likewise joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine just persons, which need no repentance.
translations.ylt: `I say to you, that so joy shall be in the heaven over one sinner reforming, rather than over ninety-nine righteous men, who have no need of reformation.
translations.web: I tell you that even so there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, than over ninety-nine righteous people who need no repentance.

translations.kjv: Either what woman having ten pieces of silver, if she lose one piece, doth not light a candle, and sweep the house, and seek diligently till she find it?
translations.ylt: `Or what woman having ten drachms, if she may lose one drachm, doth not light a lamp, and sweep the house, and seek carefully till that she may find?
translations.web: “Or what woman, if she had ten drachma coins, if she lost one drachma coin, wouldn’t light a lamp, sweep the house, and seek diligently until she found it?

translations.kjv: And when she hath found it, she calleth her friends and her neighbours together, saying, Rejoice with me; for I have found the piece which I had lost.
translations.ylt: and having found, she doth call together the female friends and the neighbours, saying, Rejoice with me, for I found the drachm that I lost.
translations.web: When she has found it, she calls together her friends and neighbors, saying, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found the drachma which I had lost!’

translations.kjv: Likewise, I say unto you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth.
translations.ylt: `So I say to you, joy doth come before the messengers of God over one sinner reforming.'
translations.web: Even so, I tell you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner repenting.”

translations.kjv: And he said, A certain man had two sons:
translations.ylt: And he said, `A certain man had two sons,
translations.web: He said, “A certain man had two sons.

translations.kjv: And the younger of them said to his father, Father, give me the portion of goods that falleth to me. And he divided unto them his living.
translations.ylt: and the younger of them said to the father, Father, give me the portion of the substance falling to me, and he divided to them the living.
translations.web: The younger of them said to his father, ‘Father, give me my share of your property.’ So he divided his livelihood between them.

translations.kjv: And not many days after the younger son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance with riotous living.
translations.ylt: `And not many days after, having gathered all together, the younger son went abroad to a far country, and there he scattered his substance, living riotously;
translations.web: Not many days after, the younger son gathered all of this together and traveled into a far country. There he wasted his property with riotous living.

translations.kjv: And when he had spent all, there arose a mighty famine in that land; and he began to be in want.
translations.ylt: and he having spent all, there came a mighty famine on that country, and himself began to be in want;
translations.web: When he had spent all of it, there arose a severe famine in that country, and he began to be in need.

translations.kjv: And he went and joined himself to a citizen of that country; and he sent him into his fields to feed swine.
translations.ylt: and having gone on, he joined himself to one of the citizens of that country, and he sent him to the fields to feed swine,
translations.web: He went and joined himself to one of the citizens of that country, and he sent him into his fields to feed pigs.

translations.kjv: And he would fain have filled his belly with the husks that the swine did eat: and no man gave unto him.
translations.ylt: and he was desirous to fill his belly from the husks that the swine were eating, and no one was giving to him.
translations.web: He wanted to fill his belly with the pods that the pigs ate, but no one gave him any.

translations.kjv: And when he came to himself, he said, How many hired servants of my father’s have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger!
translations.ylt: `And having come to himself, he said, How many hirelings of my father have a superabundance of bread, and I here with hunger am perishing!
translations.web: But when he came to himself, he said, ‘How many hired servants of my father’s have bread enough to spare, and I’m dying with hunger!

translations.kjv: I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee,
translations.ylt: having risen, I will go on unto my father, and will say to him, Father, I did sin--to the heaven, and before thee,
translations.web: I will get up and go to my father, and will tell him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven and in your sight.

translations.kjv: And am no more worthy to be called thy son: make me as one of thy hired servants.
translations.ylt: and no more am I worthy to be called thy son; make me as one of thy hirelings.
translations.web: I am no more worthy to be called your son. Make me as one of your hired servants.”’

translations.kjv: And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.
translations.ylt: `And having risen, he went unto his own father, and he being yet far distant, his father saw him, and was moved with compassion, and having ran he fell upon his neck and kissed him;
translations.web: “He arose and came to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him and was moved with compassion, and ran, fell on his neck, and kissed him.

translations.kjv: And the son said unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in thy sight, and am no more worthy to be called thy son.
translations.ylt: and the son said to him, Father, I did sin--to the heaven, and before thee, and no more am I worthy to be called thy son.
translations.web: The son said to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and in your sight. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’

translations.kjv: But the father said to his servants, Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet:
translations.ylt: `And the father said unto his servants, Bring forth the first robe, and clothe him, and give a ring for his hand, and sandals for the feet;
translations.web: “But the father said to his servants, ‘Bring out the best robe and put it on him. Put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet.

translations.kjv: And bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry:
translations.ylt: and having brought the fatted calf, kill it, and having eaten, we may be merry,
translations.web: Bring the fattened calf, kill it, and let’s eat and celebrate;

translations.kjv: For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry.
translations.ylt: because this my son was dead, and did live again, and he was lost, and was found; and they began to be merry.
translations.web: for this, my son, was dead and is alive again. He was lost and is found.’ Then they began to celebrate.

translations.kjv: Now his elder son was in the field: and as he came and drew nigh to the house, he heard musick and dancing.
translations.ylt: `And his elder son was in a field, and as, coming, he drew nigh to the house, he heard music and dancing,
translations.web: “Now his elder son was in the field. As he came near to the house, he heard music and dancing.

translations.kjv: And he called one of the servants, and asked what these things meant.
translations.ylt: and having called near one of the young men, he was inquiring what these things might be,
translations.web: He called one of the servants to him and asked what was going on.

translations.kjv: And he said unto him, Thy brother is come; and thy father hath killed the fatted calf, because he hath received him safe and sound.
translations.ylt: and he said to him--Thy brother is arrived, and thy father did kill the fatted calf, because in health he did receive him back.
translations.web: He said to him, ‘Your brother has come, and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has received him back safe and healthy.’

translations.kjv: And he was angry, and would not go in: therefore came his father out, and intreated him.
translations.ylt: `And he was angry, and would not go in, therefore his father, having come forth, was entreating him;
translations.web: But he was angry and would not go in. Therefore his father came out and begged him.

translations.kjv: And he answering said to his father, Lo, these many years do I serve thee, neither transgressed I at any time thy commandment: and yet thou never gavest me a kid, that I might make merry with my friends:
translations.ylt: and he answering said to the father, Lo, so many years I do serve thee, and never thy command did I transgress, and to me thou didst never give a kid, that with my friends I might make merry;
translations.web: But he answered his father, ‘Behold, these many years I have served you, and I never disobeyed a commandment of yours, but you never gave me a goat, that I might celebrate with my friends.

translations.kjv: But as soon as this thy son was come, which hath devoured thy living with harlots, thou hast killed for him the fatted calf.
translations.ylt: but when thy son--this one who did devour thy living with harlots--came, thou didst kill to him the fatted calf.
translations.web: But when this your son came, who has devoured your living with prostitutes, you killed the fattened calf for him.’

translations.kjv: And he said unto him, Son, thou art ever with me, and all that I have is thine.
translations.ylt: `And he said to him, Child, thou art always with me, and all my things are thine;
translations.web: “He said to him, ‘Son, you are always with me, and all that is mine is yours.

translations.kjv: It was meet that we should make merry, and be glad: for this thy brother was dead, and is alive again; and was lost, and is found.
translations.ylt: but to be merry, and to be glad, it was needful, because this thy brother was dead, and did live again, he was lost, and was found.'
translations.web: But it was appropriate to celebrate and be glad, for this, your brother, was dead, and is alive again. He was lost, and is found.’”

translations.kjv: And he said also unto his disciples, There was a certain rich man, which had a steward; and the same was accused unto him that he had wasted his goods.
translations.ylt: And he said also unto his disciples, `A certain man was rich, who had a steward, and he was accused to him as scattering his goods;
translations.web: He also said to his disciples, “There was a certain rich man who had a manager. An accusation was made to him that this man was wasting his possessions.

translations.kjv: And he called him, and said unto him, How is it that I hear this of thee? give an account of thy stewardship; for thou mayest be no longer steward.
translations.ylt: and having called him, he said to him, What is this I hear about thee? render the account of thy stewardship, for thou mayest not any longer be steward.
translations.web: He called him, and said to him, ‘What is this that I hear about you? Give an accounting of your management, for you can no longer be manager.’

translations.kjv: Then the steward said within himself, What shall I do? for my lord taketh away from me the stewardship: I cannot dig; to beg I am ashamed.
translations.ylt: `And the steward said in himself, What shall I do, because my lord doth take away the stewardship from me? to dig I am not able, to beg I am ashamed: --
translations.web: “The manager said within himself, ‘What will I do, seeing that my lord is taking away the management position from me? I don’t have strength to dig. I am ashamed to beg.

translations.kjv: I am resolved what to do, that, when I am put out of the stewardship, they may receive me into their houses.
translations.ylt: I have known what I shall do, that, when I may be removed from the stewardship, they may receive me to their houses.
translations.web: I know what I will do, so that when I am removed from management, they may receive me into their houses.’

translations.kjv: So he called every one of his lord’s debtors unto him, and said unto the first, How much owest thou unto my lord?
translations.ylt: `And having called near each one of his lord's debtors, he said to the first, How much dost thou owe to my lord?
translations.web: Calling each one of his lord’s debtors to him, he said to the first, ‘How much do you owe to my lord?’

translations.kjv: And he said, An hundred measures of oil. And he said unto him, Take thy bill, and sit down quickly, and write fifty.
translations.ylt: and he said, A hundred baths of oil; and he said to him, Take thy bill, and having sat down write fifty.
translations.web: He said, ‘A hundred batos of oil.’ He said to him, ‘Take your bill, and sit down quickly and write fifty.’

translations.kjv: Then said he to another, And how much owest thou? And he said, An hundred measures of wheat. And he said unto him, Take thy bill, and write fourscore.
translations.ylt: `Afterward to another he said, And thou, how much dost thou owe? and he said, A hundred cors of wheat; and he saith to him, Take thy bill, and write eighty.
translations.web: Then he said to another, ‘How much do you owe?’ He said, ‘A hundred cors of wheat.’ He said to him, ‘Take your bill, and write eighty.’

translations.kjv: And the lord commended the unjust steward, because he had done wisely: for the children of this world are in their generation wiser than the children of light.
translations.ylt: `And the lord commended the unrighteous steward that he did prudently, because the sons of this age are more prudent than the sons of the light, in respect to their generation.
translations.web: “His lord commended the dishonest manager because he had done wisely, for the children of this world are, in their own generation, wiser than the children of the light.

translations.kjv: And I say unto you, Make to yourselves friends of the mammon of unrighteousness; that, when ye fail, they may receive you into everlasting habitations.
translations.ylt: and I say to you, Make to yourselves friends out of the mammon of unrighteousness, that when ye may fail, they may receive you to the age-during tabernacles.
translations.web: I tell you, make for yourselves friends by means of unrighteous mammon, so that when you fail, they may receive you into the eternal tents.

translations.kjv: He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much.
translations.ylt: `He who is faithful in the least, is also faithful in much; and he who in the least is unrighteous, is also unrighteous in much;
translations.web: He who is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much. He who is dishonest in a very little is also dishonest in much.

translations.kjv: If therefore ye have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will commit to your trust the true riches?
translations.ylt: if, then, in the unrighteous mammon ye became not faithful--the true who will entrust to you?
translations.web: If therefore you have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will commit to your trust the true riches?

translations.kjv: And if ye have not been faithful in that which is another man’s, who shall give you that which is your own?
translations.ylt: and if in the other's ye became not faithful--your own, who shall give to you?
translations.web: If you have not been faithful in that which is another’s, who will give you that which is your own?

translations.kjv: No servant can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.
translations.ylt: `No domestic is able to serve two lords, for either the one he will hate, and the other he will love; or one he will hold to, and of the other he will be heedless; ye are not able to serve God and mammon.'
translations.web: No servant can serve two masters, for either he will hate the one and love the other; or else he will hold to one and despise the other. You aren’t able to serve God and Mammon.”

translations.kjv: And the Pharisees also, who were covetous, heard all these things: and they derided him.
translations.ylt: And also the Pharisees, being lovers of money, were hearing all these things, and were deriding him,
translations.web: The Pharisees, who were lovers of money, also heard all these things, and they scoffed at him.

translations.kjv: And he said unto them, Ye are they which justify yourselves before men; but God knoweth your hearts: for that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God.
translations.ylt: and he said to them, `Ye are those declaring yourselves righteous before men, but God doth know your hearts; because that which among men is high, is abomination before God;
translations.web: He said to them, “You are those who justify yourselves in the sight of men, but God knows your hearts. For that which is exalted among men is an abomination in the sight of God.

translations.kjv: The law and the prophets were until John: since that time the kingdom of God is preached, and every man presseth into it.
translations.ylt: the law and the prophets are till John; since then the reign of God is proclaimed good news, and every one doth press into it;
translations.web: “The law and the prophets were until John. From that time the Good News of God’s Kingdom is preached, and everyone is forcing his way into it.

translations.kjv: And it is easier for heaven and earth to pass, than one tittle of the law to fail.
translations.ylt: and it is easier to the heaven and the earth to pass away, than of the law one tittle to fall.
translations.web: But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for one tiny stroke of a pen in the law to fall.

translations.kjv: Whosoever putteth away his wife, and marrieth another, committeth adultery: and whosoever marrieth her that is put away from her husband committeth adultery.
translations.ylt: `Every one who is sending away his wife, and marrying another, doth commit adultery; and every one who is marrying her sent away from a husband doth commit adultery.
translations.web: “Everyone who divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery. He who marries one who is divorced from a husband commits adultery.

translations.kjv: There was a certain rich man, which was clothed in purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously every day:
translations.ylt: `And--a certain man was rich, and was clothed in purple and fine linen, making merry sumptuously every day,
translations.web: “Now there was a certain rich man, and he was clothed in purple and fine linen, living in luxury every day.

translations.kjv: And there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, which was laid at his gate, full of sores,
translations.ylt: and there was a certain poor man, by name Lazarus, who was laid at his porch, full of sores,
translations.web: A certain beggar, named Lazarus, was taken to his gate, full of sores,

translations.kjv: And desiring to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man’s table: moreover the dogs came and licked his sores.
translations.ylt: and desiring to be filled from the crumbs that are falling from the table of the rich man; yea, also the dogs, coming, were licking his sores.
translations.web: and desiring to be fed with the crumbs that fell from the rich man’s table. Yes, even the dogs came and licked his sores.

translations.kjv: And it came to pass, that the beggar died, and was carried by the angels into Abraham’s bosom: the rich man also died, and was buried;
translations.ylt: `And it came to pass, that the poor man died, and that he was carried away by the messengers to the bosom of Abraham--and the rich man also died, and was buried;
translations.web: The beggar died, and he was carried away by the angels to Abraham’s bosom. The rich man also died and was buried.

translations.kjv: And in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments, and seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom.
translations.ylt: and in the hades having lifted up his eyes, being in torments, he doth see Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom,
translations.web: In Hades, he lifted up his eyes, being in torment, and saw Abraham far off, and Lazarus at his bosom.

translations.kjv: And he cried and said, Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame.
translations.ylt: and having cried, he said, Father Abraham, deal kindly with me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and may cool my tongue, because I am distressed in this flame.
translations.web: He cried and said, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue! For I am in anguish in this flame.’

translations.kjv: But Abraham said, Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted, and thou art tormented.
translations.ylt: `And Abraham said, Child, remember that thou did receive--thou--thy good things in thy life, and Lazarus in like manner the evil things, and now he is comforted, and thou art distressed;
translations.web: “But Abraham said, ‘Son, remember that you, in your lifetime, received your good things, and Lazarus, in the same way, bad things. But here he is now comforted and you are in anguish.

translations.kjv: And beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot; neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence.
translations.ylt: and besides all these things, between us and you a great chasm is fixed, so that they who are willing to go over from hence unto you are not able, nor do they from thence to us pass through.
translations.web: Besides all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed, that those who want to pass from here to you are not able, and that no one may cross over from there to us.’

translations.kjv: Then he said, I pray thee therefore, father, that thou wouldest send him to my father’s house:
translations.ylt: `And he said, I pray thee, then, father, that thou mayest send him to the house of my father,
translations.web: “He said, ‘I ask you therefore, father, that you would send him to my father’s house—

translations.kjv: For I have five brethren; that he may testify unto them, lest they also come into this place of torment.
translations.ylt: for I have five brothers, so that he may thoroughly testify to them, that they also may not come to this place of torment.
translations.web: for I have five brothers—that he may testify to them, so they won’t also come into this place of torment.’

translations.kjv: Abraham saith unto him, They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.
translations.ylt: `Abraham saith to him, They have Moses and the prophets, let them hear them;
translations.web: “But Abraham said to him, ‘They have Moses and the prophets. Let them listen to them.’

translations.kjv: And he said, Nay, father Abraham: but if one went unto them from the dead, they will repent.
translations.ylt: and he said, No, father Abraham, but if any one from the dead may go unto them, they will reform.
translations.web: “He said, ‘No, father Abraham, but if one goes to them from the dead, they will repent.’

translations.kjv: And he said unto him, If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.
translations.ylt: And he said to him, If Moses and the prophets they do not hear, neither if one may rise out of the dead will they be persuaded.'
translations.web: “He said to him, ‘If they don’t listen to Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded if one rises from the dead.’”

translations.kjv: Then said he unto the disciples, It is impossible but that offences will come: but woe unto him, through whom they come!
translations.ylt: And he said unto the disciples, `It is impossible for the stumbling blocks not to come, but woe to him through whom they come;
translations.web: He said to the disciples, “It is impossible that no occasions of stumbling should come, but woe to him through whom they come!

translations.kjv: It were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and he cast into the sea, than that he should offend one of these little ones.
translations.ylt: it is more profitable to him if a weighty millstone is put round about his neck, and he hath been cast into the sea, than that he may cause one of these little ones to stumble.
translations.web: It would be better for him if a millstone were hung around his neck, and he were thrown into the sea, rather than that he should cause one of these little ones to stumble.

translations.kjv: Take heed to yourselves: If thy brother trespass against thee, rebuke him; and if he repent, forgive him.
translations.ylt: `Take heed to yourselves, and, if thy brother may sin in regard to thee, rebuke him, and if he may reform, forgive him,
translations.web: Be careful. If your brother sins against you, rebuke him. If he repents, forgive him.

translations.kjv: And if he trespass against thee seven times in a day, and seven times in a day turn again to thee, saying, I repent; thou shalt forgive him.
translations.ylt: and if seven times in the day he may sin against thee, and seven times in the day may turn back to thee, saying, I reform; thou shalt forgive him.'
translations.web: If he sins against you seven times in the day, and seven times returns, saying, ‘I repent,’ you shall forgive him.”

translations.kjv: And the apostles said unto the Lord, Increase our faith.
translations.ylt: And the apostles said to the Lord, `Add to us faith;'
translations.web: The apostles said to the Lord, “Increase our faith.”

translations.kjv: And the Lord said, If ye had faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye might say unto this sycamine tree, Be thou plucked up by the root, and be thou planted in the sea; and it should obey you.
translations.ylt: and the Lord said, `If ye had faith as a grain of mustard, ye would have said to this sycamine, Be uprooted, and be planted in the sea, and it would have obeyed you.
translations.web: The Lord said, “If you had faith like a grain of mustard seed, you would tell this sycamore tree, ‘Be uprooted and be planted in the sea,’ and it would obey you.

translations.kjv: But which of you, having a servant plowing or feeding cattle, will say unto him by and by, when he is come from the field, Go and sit down to meat?
translations.ylt: `But, who is he of you--having a servant ploughing or feeding--who, to him having come in out of the field, will say, Having come near, recline at meat?
translations.web: But who is there among you, having a servant plowing or keeping sheep, that will say when he comes in from the field, ‘Come immediately and sit down at the table’?

translations.kjv: And will not rather say unto him, Make ready wherewith I may sup, and gird thyself, and serve me, till I have eaten and drunken; and afterward thou shalt eat and drink?
